holidays.name: National Cheese Fondue Day
holidays.description: A celebration of dunking bread, veggies, and anything else within reach into a communal pot of molten, bubbling cheese. Double-dipping is, of course, a serious social offense.
holidays.origin: Fondue traces back to 18th-century Switzerland, where peasants stretched cheese and stale bread through the winter. The Swiss Cheese Union promoted it as a national dish in the 1930s, and the American food-holiday calendar later claimed April 11 for it.
holidays.funFact: In traditional Swiss custom, if a woman loses her bread in the pot she must kiss the person next to her, and if a man loses his, he buys the next round of drinks.

holidays.name: National Pet Day
holidays.description: A day to shower your furry, scaly, or feathered roommates with extra treats, cuddles, and photo shoots, and to encourage adoption from shelters.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2006 by animal welfare advocate and pet lifestyle expert Colleen Paige, who also created National Dog Day. It aims to promote pet adoption and honor the bond between humans and animals.
holidays.funFact: Colleen Paige chose to celebrate all pets, not just dogs and cats, so hamsters, lizards, and even pet rocks are technically invited to the party.

holidays.name: Barbershop Quartet Day
holidays.description: A day to harmonize in four-part a cappella, preferably in matching striped vests and straw hats, and to honor the close-harmony tradition.
holidays.origin: The date marks the founding of the Barbershop Harmony Society (originally the SPEBSQSA) on April 11, 1938, in Tulsa, Oklahoma, by Owen C. Cash, after a gathering on a hotel rooftop that drew 26 men.
holidays.funFact: The original society's name, Society for the Preservation and Encouragement of Barber Shop Quartet Singing in America, was a joking acronym: SPEBSQSA, which members playfully lampooned as a parody of alphabet-soup New Deal agencies.

holidays.name: World Parkinson's Day
holidays.description: An international awareness day dedicated to understanding Parkinson's disease, supporting patients and caregivers, and funding research. It is marked by red tulips and community events worldwide.
holidays.origin: The date honors the birthday of Dr. James Parkinson, who described the condition in his 1817 'An Essay on the Shaking Palsy.' The day was first marked in 1997 by the European Parkinson's Disease Association.
holidays.funFact: The red tulip became the symbol after a Dutch horticulturist with Parkinson's developed a new tulip variety in 1980 and named it after Dr. Parkinson.

holidays.name: Eight Track Tape Day
holidays.description: A nostalgic salute to the chunky, endlessly looping music cartridges of the 1960s and 70s, famous for songs fading out mid-tune while the track changed with a loud clunk.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance is a retro-tech fan celebration of the 8-track format, which was developed by Bill Lear (of Learjet fame) in the mid-1960s and popularized in cars.
holidays.funFact: Many 8-track tapes split albums in odd places, so songs were sometimes faded out and resumed after the track change, which irked some artists enough to rearrange their album track orders.
